title: Truthfulness of Scripture
definition: The truthfulness of Scripture means that God's Word is true in all that it teaches because the God who speaks cannot lie.
summary: Scripture can be trusted because its source is the faithful and truthful God. The believer is called to receive the Word as truth and reject falsehood.
christFocus: Jesus prayed, 'Your word is truth,' and He Himself is the truth to whom the Scriptures point.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Truthfulness of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to truthfulness of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
